mentions.name: dia
mentions.description: A programming language called dia ("do it all") designed as a batteries-included language with standard libraries, so software can be built with or without AI assistance while reusing building blocks instead of reimplementing them. Features include Rust-inspired syntax and type features with arena-based memory safety (no lifetime parameters), a cross-platform GUI library with a prosemirror-like WYSIWYG text editor, modular UI components (text rendering, event/input system, signals-based reactive library) reusable in other contexts, transpilation to C for broad platform support, a native JSX-like syntax (DSX) usable with any suitably signed function, incremental compilation with HMR, and effortless C interop via a bundled clang compiler. Not yet open-sourced.
mentions.problem: Developers have to reimplement building blocks; the language aims to make building with or without AI assistance effortless by including batteries and reusable modules.
